text: The user wants a short proposal first and no edits, commits or pushes until the owner approves.
Keep agent runs lean: one simple reviewer, and state the token cost in every proposal.
Never use emojis in commit messages, code comments or reports.
Commit messages follow the conventional style, for example feat(007): or fix(retrieval):.
Reports start with the verdict in the first sentence, without greetings or filler.
Cite code as file path plus line number instead of describing it vaguely.
Prefer the standard library over adding a new dependency for a few lines of code.
Never use pkill -f from the agent shell; it killed the shell once.
Run every test command under timeout so a hanging test cannot block the session.
Never git push without being asked.
Use pnpm, not npm or yarn, in JavaScript projects.
Answer in plain English with short sentences.
Mark unverified claims with [UNVERIFIED HYPOTHESIS] and name the command that would prove them.
The owner reviews YOUR-CHOICE decisions only in the final pull request.
Put temporary files in the session scratchpad, never in the project tree.
The TEI embedder runs on 127.0.0.1:18300 and serves SKILLRET-Embedding-0.6B with 1024-dimensional vectors.
The bge reranker runs in TEI on port 18301.
llama-server on port 18302 serves Qwen2.5-3B with one slot and a 32768-token context.
The scratch Postgres for the new stack is the container ctc-dev-pg on 127.0.0.1:18304.
The scratch Redis is ctc-scratch-redis on 127.0.0.1:18395.
The live Python daemon on port 18310 may only receive read-only requests and must never be restarted.
Dev runs of the new stack use CTC_HOME=.ctc-dev and port 18410 for the web process.
Supabase is never touched during the 007 build.
Never write to the real ~/.claude settings, skills or hooks from a build task.
TEI accepts at most 32 inputs per /embed request.
The toolchain is pinned to Node 22.22.1 and pnpm 10.34.5; do not install Node 24.
TypeScript runs as source through Node type stripping, with no dist build.
Tests run with Vitest 4, and lint runs ESLint 10 plus tsc --noEmit.
ESLint bans pg and kysely imports outside packages/shared/repositories.
The pnpm workspace covers apps/* and packages/* only; the dashboard stays standalone.
Python code runs through uv, which creates .venv inside the worktree.
packages/core is pure and does no I/O; the apps wire it to stores.
Zod 4 validates routes, MCP tools, queue payloads and YAML config.
The SQL layer is Kysely on pg; Prisma was rejected.
createDb installs the CamelCasePlugin, so rows come back with camelCase keys like reinforcementDates.
Each task gets a planner that writes SPEC.md, DECISIONS.md, PROCESS.md, checks.mjs and selfcheck.py under agent/<task>/.
The coder may change only the module paths that SPEC.md allows plus new test files.
Every decision line is tagged FROM-OWNER, FROM-SPEC, FROM-CALLERS or YOUR-CHOICE.
The owner accepted every planner default under O11 while asleep.
A task branch is cut from dangnguyenducanh/ctc-007-build and merged back into it.
The selfcheck prints SELFCHECK: DONE as its last line only when a full run passed.
A defect that traces to the decision list is fixed in the list, never patched into the coder's code.
Never show the coder the reference module, hidden tests or earlier run reports.
The contract files are frozen with a .contract.sha256 file that the selfcheck verifies.
The schema-assumptions test is red on the base branch because the migrations lack projects.graph_epoch and mem_epoch.
Write bands: similarity of at least 0.95 is NOOP, 0.85 to 0.95 is UPDATE or SUPERSEDE, and below 0.85 is ADD.
A NOOP appends today to reinforcement_dates at most once.
The llama judge decides same meaning versus contradicts only inside the 0.85 to 0.95 band.
An invalid llama reply is retried once with a fresh prompt and then dropped with bad_reply.
The session summary has six fields: request, investigated, learned, completed, next_steps and notes.
The summary content hash is sha256 of the summary input, not of the model reply.
llm.extract reads only the user's own typed words, never assistant text or tool output.
There is no extract cursor, so each Stop re-reads the newest 12000 characters of user words.
Spool files are written as .tmp and renamed, and a corrupt file moves to spool/corrupt/.
The spool hook nudges POST /v1/spool/nudge with a 250 ms timeout and always exits 0.
Spool files the web cannot deliver are kept for 7 days.
The SessionStart block must stay within 10000 characters and the hook has a 1200 ms budget.
Recall fuses the full-text and vector legs with reciprocal rank fusion, k = 60 and 100 per leg.
The recall score decays with a 30-day half-life and is doubled for pinned memories.
mem_epoch is a per-project token that every memory write rotates.
sanitize strips private, system-reminder and persisted-output blocks and lines that start with the ctc prefix.
Runner sessions are recognised by a cwd under /.ctc/wt/ and are never extracted.
The prompt hook has a 140 ms budget with curl -m 0.15.
The prompt line is at most 400 characters: task, file and symbol, skill and decision.
web-tree-sitter WASM grammars parse code files for the context graph.
The graph walk is a BFS of depth 2 with a hub cut-off and a 0.5 decay per hop.
A graph rebuild rotates graph_epoch so cached prompt lines die without a key scan.
The PreToolUse hook has a 50 ms budget and returns additionalContext JSON or nothing.
Doc extraction for the graph calls claude -p with the haiku model.
The skill library stores each served version of a skill with labels such as production.
get_capability and load_capability_resource are the MCP pair that reads one skill version and its files.
Skill retrieval takes dense 50 plus keyword 50 fused by RRF, reranks the top 20 and keeps 5.
The skillret document text is name, description and body capped at 8000 characters.
Workflow steps run claude -p --output-format stream-json or codex exec.
Worktrees for workflow steps live in <repo>/.ctc/wt/<run>/<step> and are kept 7 days.
Fan-out runs at most 3 children at once with depth 1.
A step report from an old attempt is refused with stale_attempt.
BullMQ runs seven queues: graph, library, llm, memory, runner, cleanup and dlq-retry.
The llm queue retries once and then writes jobs.error.
dlq-retry re-runs each failed job up to 5 times, every 10 minutes.
The L2 Redis cache has a 20 ms timeout and is marked down for 10 s after a miss.
When Redis is down the worker polls the jobs table every 5 seconds.
The jobs row in Postgres is the truth; BullMQ only carries it.
JobDropped marks a job dead with the error dropped:<code>, and BullMQ does not retry it.
The rate limit is 600 requests per minute per key in a Redis fixed window.
API errors use the body {error: {code, message}} with codes like invalid, not_found and conflict.
Lists take a limit up to 500 with keyset paging on created_at and id.
Hooks never error: any failure gives the empty reply within budget.
Every repository function takes ctx with userId first, and userId never comes from a request body.
The tenancy test checks that user B reads zero of user A's rows on every repository function.
The project docs CLAUDE.md, PLAN.md and older specs were deleted on 2026-10-30; spec 007 supersedes them.
The decisions and events tables are archived to jsonl.gz and dropped, with no ClickHouse.
The baseline fixtures hold 200 prompts: 71 own prompts and 129 SkillRet prompts.
Own-transcript prompts stay local and gitignored, with a committed sha256 manifest.
The /api fixtures cover GET routes only; mutating routes are skipped.
systemd user units are written into the repo but not installed on this machine.
At the end of the build there is one pull request from ctc-007-build into staging.
T7.2 deletes the Python service only if every verification gate is green on the new stack.
The tdd skill worked well for the repositories module: tests first caught two tenancy leaks.
graphify query answered architecture questions faster than grepping raw files.
A paused Node socket never sees the peer FIN, so a test server that never answers must call s.resume().
sanitize was quadratic on nested blocks until it became a single left-to-right pass.
A pytest run over a module that opens FIFOs hung for 300 seconds without a timeout.
Two coders that agree are not proof; their differences only show silence in the decision list.
A contract transcribed from the reference implementation carried its flaws into every run.
Memory rows carry a tsvector column generated with the simple text search configuration.
The HNSW index on memories uses vector_cosine_ops.
projects.id is the first 8 hex characters of the sha256 of the project root.
The dashboard is React with Vite and has pages for Library versions, Memories and Runs.
The dashboard rework has no frontend spec, so the dashboard-e2e gate is reported as not run.
Claude memory files map type user to preference, feedback to convention, and project or reference to fact.
The worker RSS budget is 1 GB and the web RSS budget is 600 MB.
The web process exits 78 if it cannot bind within 60 seconds.
Offline evals stay in Python and call POST /v1/suggest.
The spool body format is {v: 1, event, received_at, payload}.
Prefer boring, readable code over clever code.
Merge a task only if the scope check shows that just the module and new test files changed.
Blind reviewers must not be told which solution is the reference.
The hook body is capped at 1 MB and prompt text at 20000 characters.
Idempotency keys are pruned after 30 days.
